6a2675ea940f9d204b49ee98.rationale: The setup contrasts probe-gated suppression with always-on suppression, which suggests the finding is that always-on suppression hurts: the feature probably also carries useful information on clean steps. Many interpretability papers report exactly this pattern, with gated intervention helping and ungated intervention degrading performance. Still, always-on suppression could plausibly raise performance relative to no suppression and simply do less well than gating. I lean toward it lowering performance.
